chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Abū Usāmah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a junub who sweats in his garment, or who performs ghusl and then embraces his wife and lies with her while she is menstruating or junub, and some of her sweat touches his body. He said: All of this is nothing.

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ: it has no legal effect or consequence

ai.seo_question: Does the sweat of a junub or a menstruating woman make the body or clothing impure?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that the sweat of a junub or a menstruating woman does not render the body or garment impure in the cases mentioned. It addresses matters of taharah in marital contact and indicates that such contact with sweat carries no legal consequence here.
